intent.raw_query: Edinburgh history and whisky, $2000 solo, 5 days, September 2027, from London

experiences.name: Edinburgh Castle Tour
experiences.description: Explore the iconic fortress perched on volcanic rock, home to the Scottish Crown Jewels, the Stone of Destiny, and the famous One O'Clock Gun. Dive deep into Scotland's turbulent history spanning over 1,000 years with audio guides and live interpreter sessions.

experiences.name: Scotch Whisky Experience
experiences.description: Embark on a sensory journey through Scotland's whisky-making heritage at this dedicated attraction next to the castle. Take a barrel ride through the whisky-making process, sample drams from all five whisky regions, and explore the world's largest Scotch whisky collection with over 3,500 bottles.
experiences.location: Castlehill, Royal Mile, Old Town, Edinburgh

experiences.name: Royal Mile Historical Walking Tour
experiences.description: Join a guided walking tour along Edinburgh's most famous street stretching from the Castle to the Palace of Holyroodhouse. Uncover hidden closes, medieval history, tales of plague, body snatchers, and the stories behind iconic landmarks like St Giles' Cathedral and John Knox's House.

experiences.name: Whisky Tasting at The Scotch Malt Whisky Society
experiences.description: Visit this exclusive members' club and tasting room housed in a stunning Georgian building. Enjoy a curated tasting session of rare single cask whiskies unavailable anywhere else in the world, guided by expert staff who explain the nuances of each expression and the history of Scottish distilling.

experiences.name: Underground Vaults & Mary King's Close Tour
experiences.description: Descend beneath the Royal Mile into the eerie preserved 17th-century streets and chambers of Mary King's Close. Hear stories of plague victims, ghostly apparitions, and the everyday lives of Edinburgh's historic residents in this atmospheric underground labyrinth that remained sealed for centuries.

trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Edinburgh Airport at 12:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Take the Airlink 100 bus (£4.50 one-way) from the airport to Waverley Bridge, then walk or take a short bus to your Old Town accommodation. Check in or drop off luggage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Royal Mile Historical Walking Tour — after settling in, join the free or low-cost guided walking tour along the Royal Mile (many free tours run on tips, starting near the Castle Esplanade). Get your bearings, soak in the medieval Old Town architecture, and learn the city's layered history from the Castle down to Holyrood Palace. The tour takes roughly 2 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Grassmarket area on foot — a historic square at the foot of the Castle Rock with lively pubs and budget-friendly eateries. Enjoy the atmospheric evening views of the Castle lit up above.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and snack at the airport or on the bus — skip a formal breakfast given the midday arrival.
meals.lunch: Bite to eat near your hotel on arrival — try Greggs or a local bakery on the Royal Mile for a budget Scotch pie or sandwich (under £5).
meals.dinner: The Grassmarket — try Mum's Great Comfort Food (hearty Scottish comfort food, mains from £8–£12) or grab fish and chips from a nearby chippy for under £8.

day_by_day.notes: Airlink 100 bus from Edinburgh Airport to city centre runs every 10 minutes and takes about 30 minutes. Validate your budget by keeping Day 1 spend light — you've just arrived. Free walking tours typically depart at 11:00, 13:00, and 15:00; aim for the 14:30–15:00 slot after dropping luggage.

day_by_day.morning: Edinburgh Castle Tour — head up the Royal Mile first thing to beat the crowds. Book tickets in advance online to save a few pounds (adult entry approx. £17–£19). Spend 2–3 hours exploring the Crown Jewels, the Stone of Destiny, St Margaret's Chapel (the oldest building in Edinburgh), and sweeping panoramic views of the city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Scotch Whisky Experience — located right next to the Castle on Castlehill, this is a perfect post-Castle stop. The Silver Tour (approx. £17) includes a barrel ride through whisky history, a tutored nosing session, and a dram of your chosen Scotch. Budget-friendly and deeply educational for whisky lovers.
day_by_day.evening: Walk down the Royal Mile and explore the closes (narrow alleyways) independently — free self-guided exploration. End the evening at a traditional Old Town pub for a local cask ale or a budget dram.

meals.breakfast: Brew Lab Coffee on South College Street or a supermarket (Tesco Express on South Bridge) — coffee and pastry for under £4.
meals.lunch: Canteen at the Scotch Whisky Experience or a packed lunch from a nearby supermarket. Alternatively, The Elephant House café (birthplace of Harry Potter) offers soups and sandwiches from £6–£8.
meals.dinner: The Royal McGregor pub on the Royal Mile — hearty Scottish pub food (haggis, neeps & tatties) for around £10–£13. Great atmosphere and good value.

day_by_day.notes: Book Edinburgh Castle tickets online in advance to avoid queues and potentially save on booking fees. The Scotch Whisky Experience is steps from the Castle — combine both in one uphill morning/afternoon block to minimise walking. Wear comfortable shoes; the Royal Mile is cobblestoned.

day_by_day.morning: Underground Vaults & Mary King's Close Tour — descend beneath the Royal Mile into the preserved 17th-century underground streets. Book the Real Mary King's Close tour in advance (approx. £17–£19). This immersive guided experience covers plague history, the lives of Edinburgh's poor, and the eerie atmosphere of the sealed-off chambers. Takes about 1 hour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arthur's Seat hike — a free and rewarding afternoon activity. Walk from the Old Town to Holyrood Park (15 minutes on foot) and hike up the ancient volcano. The summit at 251m offers spectacular 360-degree views over Edinburgh and the Firth of Forth. Allow 1.5–2 hours for the round trip. A perfect budget activity costing nothing.
day_by_day.evening: Whisky bar crawl on the Royal Mile and Canongate — visit The Whiski Rooms (excellent selection of single malts, drams from £4–£8) and Cadenhead's Whisky Shop & Tasting Room (buy a bottle or sample from independent bottlers at excellent value).

meals.breakfast: Sainsbury's Local on the Royal Mile or a café — porridge or a full Scottish roll for under £5.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from a supermarket to enjoy on Arthur's Seat — sandwiches, crisps, and a drink for under £5. Alternatively, grab a takeaway from a nearby café before heading to Holyrood.
meals.dinner: Mosque Kitchen on Nicholson Street — legendary Edinburgh budget spot. Generous portions of curry, rice, and naan for around £6–£8. Cash preferred, always busy, always worth it.

day_by_day.notes: Mary King's Close tours sell out quickly — book online at least a day ahead. Arthur's Seat can be slippery in wet weather; wear sturdy shoes and bring a waterproof layer as September weather in Edinburgh is unpredictable. The hike is free and one of the best experiences in the city.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Scottish Parliament and Palace of Holyroodhouse area — the Parliament building offers free entry to the public gallery and exhibition (book a free timed ticket online). Learn about Scottish devolution and admire the striking contemporary architecture. Then walk the exterior of Holyroodhouse (entry to the Palace is £17 but exterior and gardens are viewable for free).
day_by_day.afternoon: Grassmarket and Greyfriars Kirkyard — wander the historic Grassmarket market area, browse independent shops, and then visit Greyfriars Kirkyard (free entry), one of Edinburgh's most atmospheric graveyards. See the grave of Greyfriars Bobby and spot real-life inspirations for Harry Potter characters on the headstones. Nearby Greyfriars Bobby statue is a beloved free photo stop.
day_by_day.evening: Live traditional Scottish music session (ceilidh or folk session) — many Old Town pubs host free live music on Friday evenings. The Royal Oak on Infirmary Street is famous for its nightly folk sessions (free entry, just buy a drink). A fantastic, authentic, and budget-friendly cultural experience.

meals.breakfast: Peter's Yard on Quartermile — Swedish-style bakery with excellent coffee and pastries from £3–£5. A short walk from the Old Town.
meals.lunch: Mums Great Comfort Food in the Grassmarket area — classic Scottish comfort dishes like mince and tatties or a roll and square sausage for £8–£11.
meals.dinner: The Scran & Scallie (gastropub in Stockbridge, short bus ride) for upscale-but-affordable Scottish pub food — OR stay local with a takeaway curry from Spice Garden on Nicolson Street (under £10). End the evening at The Royal Oak for the folk session.

day_by_day.notes: The Scottish Parliament free exhibition is genuinely interesting for history lovers — book the free ticket online in advance. Friday evenings are lively in Edinburgh's Old Town; the folk music scene is vibrant and welcoming to visitors. Keep an eye on The List (list.co.uk) for any free Friday night events or festivals happening in the city.

day_by_day.morning: National Museum of Scotland on Chambers Street — completely free entry. One of the best free museums in the UK. Spend 2–3 hours exploring Scottish history from Pictish stones and Viking artefacts to the Industrial Revolution and modern Scotland. Don't miss the rooftop terrace for panoramic Old Town views (free access).
day_by_day.afternoon: Whisky shopping and the Cowgate/Southside — visit Cadenhead's Whisky Shop on Canongate for independent bottlings at excellent prices (bottles from £25–£40 for quality single malts — far cheaper than airport or tourist shops). Browse the Victoria Street area (the curved, colourful street said to inspire Diagon Alley) and the Grassmarket one last time. Pick up any souvenirs from independent shops rather than tourist traps.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner and a final dram — treat yourself to a slightly more indulgent last dinner while staying within budget.

meals.breakfast: Full Scottish breakfast at a local café — try The Pantry on Queensferry Street or a café near your hotel. A full fry-up with coffee for £8–£10 is a proper send-off meal.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the National Museum of Scotland café — soup and a sandwich for £6–£8, or bring your own snacks to the museum (eating allowed in designated areas).
meals.dinner: The Albanach on the Royal Mile — Scottish pub with good whisky selection and a solid menu. Alternatively, Howies Restaurant (£12–£18 mains) for a special last-night Scottish dinner with haggis, venison, or fresh Scottish salmon. Finish with a farewell dram at The Bow Bar on West Bow — one of Edinburgh's finest traditional pubs with an exceptional whisky selection and drams from £4.

day_by_day.notes: The National Museum of Scotland is free and absolutely not to be missed — budget a good 2–3 hours minimum. Cadenhead's is the oldest independent whisky bottler in Scotland and offers far better value than airport duty-free for taking home a bottle. Saturday is the busiest day on the Royal Mile — visit popular spots early. Check your return travel arrangements and factor in travel time back to the airport (Airlink 100 bus, allow 45–60 minutes including walk to bus stop).

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Edinburgh Airport at 12:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Take the Airlink 100 bus or tram into the city centre (~30 min). Check in to your Old Town hotel and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Royal Mile Historical Walking Tour: After settling in, join an afternoon guided walking tour along the Royal Mile, stretching from Edinburgh Castle down to the Palace of Holyroodhouse. Learn about centuries of Scottish history, architecture, and local legends from a knowledgeable guide. The tour departs from the Castlehill end and takes approximately 2 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Grassmarket area on foot — a lively historic square with independent bars and restaurants. Enjoy the atmosphere of Old Town as the city lights up at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and pastry at the airport or on arrival — nothing formal scheduled given the midday landing.
meals.lunch: Deacon's House Café on the Royal Mile — a cosy mid-range spot serving hearty Scottish soups, sandwiches, and light bites, perfect for a quick refuel after arrival.
meals.dinner: The Grain Store, Victoria Street — a beloved Old Town restaurant with exposed stone walls and a seasonal Scottish menu. Mains range £16–£26. Try the haggis bon bons to start and a Scottish beef dish for mains.

day_by_day.notes: Flight lands at 12:00; allow ~1.5 hours for baggage, transport, and check-in before starting the afternoon tour. Book the Royal Mile Walking Tour in advance to secure an afternoon slot. Wear comfortable walking shoes as Old Town streets are cobbled.

day_by_day.morning: Edinburgh Castle Tour: Start the day early with a visit to the iconic fortress perched on volcanic Castle Rock. Explore the Scottish Crown Jewels, the Stone of Destiny, St Margaret's Chapel, and the Great Hall. Allow 2–3 hours to do the castle justice. Book a timed entry slot in advance to avoid queues.
day_by_day.afternoon: Scotch Whisky Experience: Head directly downhill from the Castle to this dedicated whisky attraction on the Royal Mile. Take the immersive barrel ride through Scotland's five whisky-producing regions, learn about the distilling process, and enjoy a guided nosing and tasting session. The Silver Tour (approx. £19–£22) includes a dram and is ideal for beginners and enthusiasts alike.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Victoria Street and the Cowgate for a relaxed evening. Pop into The Bow Bar on West Bow — one of Edinburgh's finest traditional pubs — for a carefully chosen dram from their extensive single malt selection.

meals.breakfast: Brew Lab Coffee on South College Street — specialty coffee and excellent pastries or avocado toast. A favourite among locals.
meals.lunch: Cannonball Restaurant & Bar, just beside the Castle Esplanade — mid-range Scottish cuisine with panoramic city views. Try the cullen skink (smoked haddock soup) for a classic Scottish lunch (£12–£18).
meals.dinner: Ondine Restaurant on George IV Bridge — a celebrated seafood restaurant with sustainably sourced Scottish fish and shellfish. Set menu options available around £35–£45 per person. Worth the modest splurge for a special evening.

day_by_day.notes: Book Edinburgh Castle tickets online well in advance — they sell out quickly, especially in September. The Scotch Whisky Experience is a 5-minute walk downhill from the Castle, making this a natural pairing. September weather can be cool and breezy on Castle Rock, so bring a light jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Underground Vaults & Mary King's Close Tour: Descend beneath the Royal Mile into the eerie preserved 17th-century streets and chambers hidden under the South Bridge and the Old Town tenements. The guided tour lasts approximately 75–90 minutes and brings Edinburgh's dark history vividly to life — plague, poverty, and the city's buried past. Book the morning slot to beat the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely afternoon walk up Arthur's Seat in Holyrood Park — the ancient volcano rising 251 metres above the city. The hike to the summit takes about 45 minutes and rewards with sweeping panoramic views of Edinburgh, the Firth of Forth, and the Highlands on clear days. Alternatively, explore the grounds of the Palace of Holyroodhouse at the foot of the Royal Mile.
day_by_day.evening: Whisky Tasting at The Scotch Malt Whisky Society (SMWS): Visit the members' tasting room at The Vaults on Giles Street (Leith) or the Queen Street parlour. Arrange a guest visit or tasting session in advance. The SMWS bottles single cask whisky under quirky names and the experience is unlike any standard tasting — a highlight for whisky enthusiasts.

meals.breakfast: The Edinburgh Larder on Blackfriars Street — a charming café serving Scottish produce-led breakfasts including porridge, eggs, and smoked salmon on toast (£8–£13).
meals.lunch: Picnic from Earthy on Canongate — a wholesome deli and café with fresh salads, sandwiches, and local produce. Enjoy your lunch in the grounds of Holyrood Park before the afternoon walk.
meals.dinner: The Kitchin in Leith (if combining with the SMWS evening visit) — a Michelin-starred restaurant by Tom Kitchin celebrating 'From Nature to Plate' Scottish cuisine. Book the tasting menu (£95pp) for a special occasion, or opt for à la carte to keep costs moderate. Alternatively, Fishers Bistro in Leith is a superb mid-range option (mains £18–£28).

day_by_day.notes: Book the Underground Vaults / Mary King's Close tour in advance — these are among Edinburgh's most popular experiences. For the SMWS, contact them ahead of your trip to arrange a non-member guest tasting session; they do accommodate visitors with advance notice. Wear sturdy shoes for Arthur's Seat — the path can be muddy in September.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Scottish National Museum on Chambers Street — free entry and one of Scotland's finest museums. Spend 2–3 hours exploring galleries covering Scottish history, science, world cultures, and art. Highlights include the Lewis Chessmen, Dolly the sheep, and the Scottish history galleries tracing the nation from Pictish times to the present.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the New Town and Princes Street Gardens: Walk north from Old Town across the Mound to the elegant Georgian New Town. Stroll along George Street and browse independent shops on Thistle Street. Visit the Scottish National Portrait Gallery on Queen Street (free entry) to see portraits of Mary Queen of Scots, Robert Burns, and other figures from Scottish history.
day_by_day.evening: Whisky Bar Crawl through the Old Town and New Town: Visit a curated selection of Edinburgh's best whisky bars. Start at The Vault Bar on Niddry Street, continue to The Devil's Advocate on Advocates Close (stunning Victorian pump-house setting), and finish at Bramble Bar on Queen Street — a cocktail bar with an outstanding whisky list. Each stop, enjoy one or two drams and compare styles across regions.

meals.breakfast: Peter's Yard on Quartermile — a Scandinavian-inspired bakery with exceptional sourdough, crispbreads, and coffee. A relaxed and affordable morning option (£7–£12).
meals.lunch: Café at the Scottish National Museum — reasonably priced café inside the museum with hot meals, sandwiches, and daily specials. Convenient and mid-range (£10–£15).
meals.dinner: The Witchery by the Castle on Castlehill — a legendary Edinburgh institution with Gothic-inspired décor and a menu of Scottish game, beef, and seafood. Two-course dinner around £40–£55pp. A dramatic and memorable setting for a Friday evening.

day_by_day.notes: The Scottish National Museum and Portrait Gallery are both free, making this a budget-friendly day for activities. The whisky bar crawl is self-guided — pace yourself and consider ordering half-drams at each stop to sample more variety without overindulging. Friday evenings in Edinburgh's Old Town are lively, so expect a vibrant atmosphere.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Greyfriars Kirkyard and the Grassmarket: Begin with a visit to the atmospheric Greyfriars Kirk and its historic churchyard — resting place of Covenanters, architects, and the legendary loyal dog Greyfriars Bobby. Spend time reading the remarkable gravestones and absorbing the history. Then wander the Grassmarket below for independent shops, vintage stores, and a final look at Old Town life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Victoria Street & Whisky Shopping: Browse the colourful curved Victoria Street — said to have inspired Diagon Alley — and visit Royal Mile Whiskies or Cadenhead's Whisky Shop on Canongate to pick up a bottle or two as souvenirs. The staff at both shops are knowledgeable and happy to recommend drams suited to your taste and budget. Spend the final afternoon soaking in the Old Town atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in the Old Town before departure preparations. Return to the hotel to pack and prepare for onward travel.

meals.breakfast: Loudons Bakehouse & Café on Fountainbridge — a beloved Edinburgh bakery with outstanding pastries, eggs, and coffee. A local favourite worth the short walk from Old Town (£8–£14).
meals.lunch: Wedgwood the Restaurant on the Royal Mile — a romantic, mid-range restaurant showcasing foraged and locally sourced Scottish ingredients. Two-course lunch around £25–£35pp. A lovely final daytime meal.
meals.dinner: The White Horse on the Royal Mile — one of Edinburgh's oldest pubs, recently restored, with a warm traditional atmosphere and a solid Scottish menu of pies, stews, and haggis. Mains £14–£22. A fitting, unpretentious farewell to Edinburgh.

day_by_day.notes: Cadenhead's Whisky Shop is the oldest independent whisky retailer in Scotland — a must-visit for enthusiasts. Check airline liquid restrictions before purchasing bottles to ensure they can be carried safely in checked luggage. If departing on the 19th, plan the evening accordingly; if the return flight is the following day, the evening is free for a final leisurely dram at The Bow Bar.

Your expert guide will bring centuries of Scottish history to life, pointing out hidden closes, medieval architecture, and stories of kings and reformers.
day_by_day.evening: Scotch Whisky Experience — Begin your whisky journey at this world-class attraction near the Castle Esplanade. Enjoy the premium barrel ride through Scotland's whisky regions, followed by an exclusive tutored tasting session featuring rare single malts from all five regions.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy a light snack or meal at the airport before departure — no Edinburgh breakfast scheduled given midday arrival.
meals.lunch: The Witchery by the Castle — Indulge in a luxurious two-course lunch in one of Edinburgh's most celebrated and atmospheric restaurants, draped in Gothic opulence just steps from the Castle gate.
meals.dinner: Ondine Restaurant — A premium seafood-focused fine dining experience on the Royal Mile. Savour sustainably sourced Scottish langoustines, oysters, and hand-dived scallops paired with an exceptional wine list.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. The Royal Mile walking tour should be pre-booked as a private guided experience for a more personalised and premium feel. Confirm Scotch Whisky Experience evening session availability. Pack layers as September evenings in Edinburgh can be cool and breezy.

day_by_day.morning: Edinburgh Castle Tour — Begin the day with a thorough private guided tour of Scotland's most iconic fortress. Explore the Scottish Crown Jewels, the Stone of Destiny, St Margaret's Chapel, the Great Hall, and panoramic views across the city. A private guide ensures priority access and deeper historical context beyond the standard visitor experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Underground Vaults & Mary King's Close Tour — Descend beneath the Royal Mile into the eerily preserved 17th-century streets and chambers of Mary King's Close. A premium private tour unlocks hidden stories of plague victims, merchants, and the city's dark underground history. This atmospheric experience perfectly complements the morning's Castle visit.
day_by_day.evening: Whisky Tasting at The Scotch Malt Whisky Society — Visit this exclusive members' club housed in a stunning Georgian building on Queen Street. Arrange a guest membership or accompanied visit for an evening of rare, cask-strength single malts unavailable anywhere else, guided by a knowledgeable SMWS ambassador.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast at your Old Town luxury accommodation — opt for a full Scottish breakfast featuring Loch Fyne smoked salmon, Stornoway black pudding, free-range eggs, and freshly baked bread.
meals.lunch: Amber Restaurant at the Scotch Whisky Experience — A natural pairing with the afternoon's theme. Enjoy refined Scottish cuisine with whisky-infused dishes such as haggis bon bons, venison tartare, and cranachan, alongside a curated whisky flight.
meals.dinner: The Printing Press Bar & Kitchen at The George Hotel — Elegant Scottish brasserie dining in a beautifully restored Georgian setting. Enjoy prime Scottish beef, seasonal game, and an impressive gin and whisky selection in refined surroundings.

day_by_day.notes: Edinburgh Castle is best visited early to avoid peak crowds — aim for a 9:30 AM entry. Pre-book the private Castle guide through a specialist tour operator. The SMWS may require advance arrangement for non-members; contact them ahead of your trip to secure a guest evening tasting slot. Comfortable walking shoes are strongly recommended for the vaults and cobblestone streets.

day_by_day.morning: Private Holyrood & Arthur's Seat Experience — Begin with a guided visit to the Palace of Holyroodhouse, the official Scottish residence of the monarch, exploring the historic State Apartments and the ruins of Holyrood Abbey. Follow with a leisurely guided walk up the lower slopes of Arthur's Seat for sweeping panoramic views over Edinburgh — a dramatic volcanic landscape steeped in geological and mythological history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Scottish Parliament Building and the Canongate Kirk area with your guide, then enjoy leisure time browsing the independent galleries and boutiques of the Grassmarket and Victoria Street — Edinburgh's most picturesque and colourful shopping street, perfect for sourcing premium Scottish cashmere, artisan whisky accessories, and fine gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Private Whisky Blending Masterclass — Book an exclusive private session with a master blender at a boutique Edinburgh whisky studio. Learn the art of nosing, blending, and bottling your very own personalised Scotch whisky blend to take home as a one-of-a-kind luxury souvenir.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast — request a lighter continental option with Scottish artisan cheeses, smoked meats, fresh fruit, and freshly squeezed juices to prepare for an active morning.
meals.lunch: The Gardener's Cottage — A charming, intimate restaurant near Holyrood using hyper-seasonal, locally grown produce in a long-table communal dining format. Pre-booking essential. A hidden gem beloved by Edinburgh food lovers.
meals.dinner: Restaurant Martin Wishart (or Number One at The Balmoral) — Treat yourself to Edinburgh's finest Michelin-starred dining. Martin Wishart offers exquisite French-influenced Scottish cuisine with impeccable service and an award-winning wine cellar. A true luxury highlight of the trip.

day_by_day.notes: Arthur's Seat walk involves some uneven terrain — wear appropriate footwear. The whisky blending masterclass should be pre-booked well in advance as private sessions fill up quickly. Martin Wishart requires advance reservation and smart dress; book as early as possible given its Michelin-starred reputation.

day_by_day.morning: Day Excursion to The Borders & a Distillery Visit — Arrange a private chauffeured excursion south of Edinburgh into the scenic Scottish Borders. Visit Glenkinchie Distillery, the 'Edinburgh Malt' and the closest Scotch whisky distillery to the city. Enjoy a premium private tour of the production facilities, warehouses, and a rare cask tasting session with the distillery manager.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the scenic Borders drive, stopping at Rosslyn Chapel — the breathtaking 15th-century masterpiece immortalised by The Da Vinci Code. A private guided tour reveals the extraordinary stone carvings, Green Men, and enduring mysteries of this remarkable building. Return to Edinburgh Old Town by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Free evening at leisure in Edinburgh's New Town — stroll along Princes Street Gardens as the sun sets over the Castle, then explore the elegant Georgian streets of the New Town, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Enjoy pre-dinner cocktails at a celebrated Edinburgh bar.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast — full Scottish option to fuel the day's excursion.
meals.lunch: Picnic hamper prepared by your hotel or a local delicatessen — enjoy a premium Scottish spread of artisan cheeses, charcuterie, oatcakes, and local preserves in the scenic Borders countryside or the grounds near Rosslyn Chapel.
meals.dinner: Café Royal — An Edinburgh institution with magnificent Victorian interiors, stained glass, and Doulton tile portraits. Enjoy an indulgent dinner of Loch Duart salmon, lobster thermidor, and Scottish oysters in one of the city's most beautiful dining rooms.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange the private chauffeured vehicle the night before. Glenkinchie is approximately 15 miles from Edinburgh city centre. Rosslyn Chapel requires advance booking for entry. The hotel concierge can organise a bespoke picnic hamper with advance notice. September light in Scotland is beautiful in the late afternoon — ideal for photography at Rosslyn.

day_by_day.morning: National Museum of Scotland — Spend a leisurely premium morning exploring this world-class free museum on Chambers Street, just minutes from the Old Town. Highlights include Dolly the Sheep, the Lewis Chessmen, ancient Pictish stones, and extensive Scottish history galleries. Arrange a private curator-led tour for an exclusive behind-the-scenes perspective unavailable to standard visitors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Calton Hill & New Town Farewell Stroll — Climb Calton Hill for sweeping 360-degree views of Edinburgh's skyline, the Firth of Forth, and Arthur's Seat. Visit the National Monument and Nelson Monument before descending into the elegant New Town for a final afternoon of luxury shopping along George Street — home to premium Scottish brands, jewellers, and whisky specialists such as Royal Mile Whiskies.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner & Whisky Nightcap — Celebrate the end of an extraordinary Edinburgh experience with a grand farewell dinner, followed by a curated whisky nightcap at one of Edinburgh's finest whisky bars.

meals.breakfast: Champagne breakfast in your hotel suite or at the hotel restaurant — a luxurious send-off to mark the final morning. Opt for smoked salmon blinis, eggs Benedict with Scottish ham, fresh pastries, and a glass of vintage Champagne.
meals.lunch: The Pompadour by Galvin at the Caledonian Waldorf Astoria — Dine in one of Edinburgh's most opulent rooms with sweeping views of the Castle. Enjoy refined Scottish-French cuisine in truly grand surroundings — a fitting final lunch.
meals.dinner: The Honours by Martin Wishart — A slightly more relaxed but equally refined brasserie from the Michelin-starred chef. Enjoy classic Scottish dishes elevated with French technique: beef tartare, Isle of Skye scallops, and a legendary sticky toffee pudding. Follow dinner with a dram at The Scotch Bar at The Balmoral — one of Edinburgh's finest hotel whisky bars, boasting over 500 expressions.

day_by_day.notes: The National Museum of Scotland private curator tour must be arranged well in advance through the museum's events team. Royal Mile Whiskies is an excellent stop for purchasing bottles of rare Scotch to take home — the staff are exceptionally knowledgeable. Confirm checkout time with your hotel and arrange a private chauffeur for any onward travel or airport transfer. September 19th is a Saturday, so the New Town will be lively — ideal for soaking up Edinburgh's vibrant atmosphere on your final evening.
